q7.answer: It lives in Redis, at one entry per connection. The ZSET `pres:conns:{doc}` holds members `userId/connId`, scored by the Redis `TIME` of the last heartbeat, and the HASH `pres:cur:{doc}` holds each connection's last cursor. Every 10 s the owning node runs the heartbeat script, which updates the score and resets the 60 s TTL on both keys; the list is still published to clients per user.

q8.answer: Any surviving node that still has sockets on the doc runs the heartbeat script every 10 s, and that script sweeps every member older than 30 s, removing it the same way a leave does (ZREM, HDEL). The script publishes `cursor_gone` and, when it was the user's last member, `presence absent` on `pres:{doc}`. Every subscribed node then forwards those events to its local clients. If no node with sockets on the doc survives, the 60 s TTL deletes both keys.

q9.answer: The sender's node checks the 50 ms limit, assigns the next `seq` and runs the cursor script. The script stores the cursor in `pres:cur:{doc}` (only while the member exists, and only if `seq` is higher) and publishes it on `pres:{doc}`. Every subscribed node forwards it to its local sockets. The sender's own node gets it back from the channel too and forwards it to its other local sockets on the doc, but skips the connection that sent it.

q10.answer: The node subscribes to `pres:{doc}` before reading anything, and queues the new connection's events. One join script registers the connection and returns the snapshot of members and cursors atomically. The node sends the snapshot, then the queued events in order, then live events. Events state absolute state and cursors carry `seq`, so a queued event the snapshot already covers is either dropped or does nothing.

q11.answer: The join snapshot includes every connection's last stored cursor from `pres:cur:{doc}`. Every client sends its caret once right after loading. An idle client also re-sends its caret every 10 s whenever its `appliedRev` has moved, which keeps stored positions close to the head revision. The joiner draws each stored caret with `transformPosition`, or holds it as pending if its revision is ahead of the joiner's `appliedRev`.

q12.answer: Each accepted cursor gets a per-connection `seq` from the one node that owns the connection. The receiver drops any update whose `seq` is not higher than the last one it saw for that `connId`. A sender's `appliedRev` only moves forward, so a higher `seq` never carries an older revision, and the pending slot only ever holds the newest update.
